title: URL Shortener
summary: A URL shortener maps a short code to a long URL. Writes are rare, while reads can be 100 times more frequent and must be very fast. Codes come from a collision-free ID generator, redirects are served from cache, and click analytics are recorded asynchronously so counting never slows a redirect down.

walkthrough.title: Create a link
walkthrough.text: POST /links { longUrl } passes the edge (auth, rate limits) to the write API, which validates the URL and checks it against malware and phishing lists.

walkthrough.title: Allocate an ID
walkthrough.text: The write API takes the next number from a block of IDs it leased earlier and base62-encodes it. Seven characters give 62^7 ≈ 3.5 trillion codes, with no collisions to check.

walkthrough.title: Store the mapping
walkthrough.text: code → { longUrl, ownerId, expiresAt } is written with a conditional put, so an existing code can never be overwritten.

walkthrough.title: Someone clicks
walkthrough.text: GET /abc1234 reaches the nearest edge location. If the CDN has the redirect cached, it answers right there.

walkthrough.title: Look up the code
walkthrough.text: The redirect service reads from Redis; on a miss it reads the database and fills the cache. Unknown codes are cached too, briefly, to stop scans from hammering the database.

walkthrough.title: Redirect and count
walkthrough.text: The service returns 302 Location: longUrl and emits a click event without waiting for it. 301 is cacheable by browsers but hides repeat clicks from analytics.

data.label: Browser / API Client
responsibilities: Creates links through the app or API with an API key.
Follows redirects; browsers cache 301s indefinitely, 302s not at all.
Shares short links in places with tight character limits (SMS, print, QR codes).

failureModes.scenario: Link scraper or scanner enumerates codes
failureModes.impact: Private links are discovered; heavy read load.
failureModes.mitigation: Non-sequential codes for private links (random or shuffled IDs); per-IP rate limits.

failureModes.scenario: Wrong 301 published and cached by browsers
failureModes.impact: Users keep going to the old destination even after it's fixed.
failureModes.mitigation: Use 302 for editable links; reserve 301 for permanent ones.

data.label: Edge / CDN & Rate Limiter
responsibilities: Terminates TLS close to users and caches redirects for popular codes for seconds to minutes.
Rate-limits link creation per API key and IP to deter spam and abuse.
Absorbs viral spikes, such as one link in a Super Bowl ad, before they reach origin.

failureModes.scenario: Edge serves a cached redirect after the link was disabled for abuse
failureModes.mitigation: Purge API call on takedown; short edge TTLs for redirects.

failureModes.scenario: Cache stampede when a hot key expires
failureModes.impact: Thousands of simultaneous misses hit origin.
failureModes.mitigation: Request coalescing and stale-while-revalidate at the edge.

data.label: Link Write API

input.name: Create
input.type: JSON: { longUrl, customAlias?, expiresAt? } + API key

output.name: Mapping
output.type: JSON: { code: "abc1234", longUrl, ownerId, createdAt, expiresAt }

responsibilities: Validates and normalizes URLs; rejects known-malicious destinations.
Base62-encodes an ID from its leased block (or checks a custom alias is free).
Optionally dedupes: the same owner and URL return the existing code.

failureModes.scenario: Spammers create links to phishing sites
failureModes.impact: The domain is blocklisted by browsers and email providers, breaking every customer's links.
failureModes.mitigation: Scan on create and re-scan periodically; fast takedown; trust tiers for new accounts.

failureModes.impact: One user overwrites the other's link.
failureModes.mitigation: Conditional insert (put-if-absent); the loser gets a 409.

data.label: ID Generator
responsibilities: Hands out disjoint ID ranges so each writer can mint codes locally without coordination.
Guarantees uniqueness without the database checks that random codes need.
Optionally scrambles IDs (e.g. a reversible bit permutation) so codes aren't guessable in sequence.

failureModes.impact: No new links once writers exhaust their current blocks.
failureModes.mitigation: Writers lease the next block early; larger blocks buy more time.
Harmless: gaps are fine, and the ID space is effectively unlimited.

data.label: Redirect Service

output.name: Click event
output.type: Event: { code, ts, country, device, referer } (fire-and-forget)

responsibilities: Resolves code → URL with a p99 target in single-digit milliseconds.
Handles expired and disabled links with clear 410 and 451 responses.
Emits click events to a local buffer and never waits on analytics.

failureModes.impact: If emitted synchronously, every redirect slows down too.
failureModes.mitigation: Bounded in-memory buffer; drop or sample events under pressure, never block the redirect.

failureModes.impact: Attackers use your trusted domain to launder phishing URLs.
failureModes.mitigation: Destination scanning, interstitial warnings for flagged links, abuse reporting.

data.label: Redirect Cache
responsibilities: Keeps the hot set of codes in memory; clicks follow a power law, so a small cache serves most traffic.
Read-through: on a miss, load from the database and populate with a TTL.
Negative-caches unknown codes to absorb enumeration and typo traffic.

failureModes.impact: The full read load hits the database, which may fall over.
failureModes.mitigation: Database sized for cold-cache load, or warm the cache from recent click logs on startup.

failureModes.scenario: Link edited but cache still holds the old URL
failureModes.impact: Visitors go to the old destination until the TTL expires.
failureModes.mitigation: Delete the cache key (and purge the edge) as part of every update.

data.label: Link Database
responsibilities: Stores billions of small records with single-key lookups only, which is a perfect fit for a key-value store.
Replicates across regions so redirects survive a regional outage.
Expires links automatically via TTL attributes.

failureModes.impact: Links created only in that region are unresolvable.
failureModes.mitigation: Multi-region replication (global tables); redirects read the local replica.

failureModes.scenario: Hot partition from one viral code
failureModes.mitigation: The cache and edge absorb it; the database should rarely see repeat reads for one code.

data.label: Click Analytics

input.name: Click events
input.type: Event: { code, ts, country, device, referer }

output.name: Stats
output.type: SQL: clicks by code × day × country × referer

responsibilities: Ingests click events in batches and aggregates them into per-link dashboards.
Filters bots and link-preview crawlers (Slack, Twitter unfurls) from human clicks.
Provides approximate unique counts (HyperLogLog) cheaply at scale.

failureModes.impact: Dashboards are stale; redirects are unaffected.
failureModes.mitigation: Buffered in Kafka; show a 'data delayed' banner instead of wrong numbers.

failureModes.impact: Customers see clicks that no human made.
failureModes.mitigation: User-agent and behaviour filtering; label preview fetches separately.
